name: Light Ochraceous-Salmon
lede: Light Ochraceous-Salmon pales [[light-orange]], a Ridgway compound joining *ochraceous* (ochre-colored) to *salmon*, and is one painter's favorite peachy tone.

sections.title: Ochre plus salmon
sections.body: The base name [[light-orange]] joins *ochraceous*, meaning ochre-colored, to *salmon*, the pink of the fish's flesh; this compound simply adds the modifier *light* [1]. It is first recorded in Robert Ridgway's 1912 *Color Standards and Nomenclature*, plate XV, hue 13', tone d, a scan of an aged plate and so an approximation [1]. The ISCC-NBS lists of 1955 file the same range as block 73, "pale orange yellow," a Delta-E of 5.4 away [1]. Nearest on file is [[sugar-cane]] at 3.2 units, with [[macaroni-and-cheese]] and [[peach]] close behind [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this tone, as photographed, in 448 of 23,781 paintings, 1.88 percent, more common than 73 percent of our named colors; within a single canvas it is a distinct area in 230 of them [2]. Pierre Puvis de Chavannes is its most devoted painter, using it in 5 of 25 works here, 6.4 times the baseline rate of the museums those paintings come from [2]. It is also most over-represented in Indian paintings in our data, 3.5 times expected, and inside a painting it most often plays a light, in 63 percent of its 230 appearances [2]. The earliest dated match is from the year 1000, 912 years before Ridgway's 1912 record; the archive's early centuries are thin, so this is a floor, not a first [2]. It shares canvases with [[antique-brass]] more often than chance, a lift of 8.5 [2].

origin.named_after: the modifiers light and ochraceous applied to the base color salmon
